'''Josiane Serre''' (17 December 1922 - 11 October 2004) was a French academic [[chemist]], the final director of the l'[[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]], and acting director of l'[[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in [[Paris]]. A French pioneer of [[quantum chemistry]],<ref name="40fs">{{cite web |url=https://www.medecinesciences.org/images/stories/news/Portraits-de-femmes-2017.pdf |title=40 fessmes scientifiques remarquables du XVIIIème siècle |publisher=Femmes & Sciences |access-date=11 June 2026 |language=French}}</ref> she is one of 72 women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to  the [[Eiffel Tower]].<ref name=":4">[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-28</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Josiane Marie Mauricette Blanche Heulot was born on 17 December 1922 in [[Lyon]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Heulot, Josiane Marie Mauricette Blanche |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/5Z_dHmLkfqeS |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=deces.matchid.io}}</ref> She earned her [[Baccalauréat|baccalauréats]] in arts and sciences in 1940, then attended preparatory classes at the [[Lycée Fénelon, Paris|lycée Fénelon]] in Paris.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |url=https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/47449d_3482c311db9042ccab4f66f61b90df9b.pdf |title=40 femmes scientifiques remarquables du XVIIIe siècle à nos jours |date=2018 |access-date=2022-03-04}}</ref> After a period of illness, in 1944 she entered the l'[[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]] in [[Sèvres]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  

Heulot passed the agrégation de sciences physiques examination in 1948<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Chervel |first=André |date=2015 |title=Les agrégés de l'enseignement secondaire. Répertoire 1809-1960 |url=http://rhe.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr/?q=agregsecondaire_laureats&annee_op==&annee%5Bvalue%5D=1948&annee%5Bmin%5D=&annee%5Bmax%5D=&nom=&periode=All&concours=15&items_per_page=10&page=2 |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=rhe.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr}}</ref><ref name="LM1975">{{Cite journal |date=1975-11-18 |title=Mme Serre est nommée directrice de l’École normale supérieure de jeunes filles |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1975/11/18/mme-serre-est-nommee-directrice-de-l-ecole-normale-superieure-de-jeunes-filles_2583949_1819218.html |journal=Le Monde |language=fr |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref> and earned a doctorate in chemistry at the [[University of Paris]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=REPERES |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1991/04/11/reperes_4010118_1819218.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603165358/https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1991/04/11/reperes_4010118_1819218.html |archive-date=2025-06-03 |access-date=2026-03-01 |work=Le Monde.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Berthelemy |first=Claire |date=28 January 2026 |title=Dans quelles écoles ont été formées les 72 scientifiques dont les noms vont orner la tour Eiffel ? |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/etudiant/etudes/ecoles/universite-de-paris-ens-medecine-dou-viennent-les-72-scientifiques-dont-les-noms-vont-orner-la-tour-eiffel-NFQ32TZMIRDITKDZOPS5RUHVLM.php |work=Le Parisien |language=fr}}</ref> After marriage to mathematician [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] she took his surname and became known as Josiane Serre.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Fonds : École normale supérieure de jeunes filles, répertoire numérique détaillé (1881-1986). Cote : FRAN_NP_003775 20160281/1-20160281/143. Paris : Archives nationales |url=https://www.siv.archives-nationales.culture.gouv.fr/siv/rechercheconsultation/consultation/ir/pdfIR.action?irId=FRAN_IR_056840}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Serre_thom_reeb_1949.jpg|left|thumb|Left to right: [[René Thom]], Jean Arbault, [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], Josiane Serre, Jean Braconnier and [[Georges Reeb]] at the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]] in 1949.|267x267px]]
She initially worked in [[organic chemistry]] at the l'[[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure de la rue d'Ulm]] where she conducted research on [[terpene]] derivatives.<ref name=":0" /> Whilst working there she suffered a serious laboratory accident in which she nearly lost the use of one hand. In January 1952, she switched to [[quantum chemistry]] at the Radium Institute, headed by [[Bernard Pullman|Bernard]] and [[Alberte Pullman]] and {{ill|Gaston Berthier|fr}}.<ref name=":0" /> Her research focused on [[acetylenic]] compounds.<ref name=":0" /> Research focusing on the new field of quantum chemistry required mathematical analyses before computer processing of the data could be undertaken. Here Serre was able to collaborate with her husband Jean-Pierre Serre.<ref name=40fs/> During the 1960s, a research group on quantum chemistry was founded at the École normale supérieure, supervised by Josiane Serre.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lipkowitz |first=Kenny B. |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Reviews_in_Computational_Chemistry_Volum/aELJb5q3hOYC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22Josiane%22+pullman+quantum+chemistry&pg=PA369&printsec=frontcover |title=Reviews in Computational Chemistry, Volume 12 |last2=Boyd |first2=Donald B. |date=2009-09-22 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-470-12616-5 |language=en}}</ref> 

After two years teaching in a [[Secondary education in France|secondary school]],<ref name=":0" /> she moved into higher education teaching in 1950 at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]] (ENSJF).<ref name=":0" /> She was successively assistant, lecturer (1961–1972), professor, deputy director (1969–1974)<ref name="LM1975" /> and finally director of the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (1974–1987).<ref name=":3" /> Serre encouraged ENSJF students to not limit themselves and to seek the same university positions as their male counterparts. She also worked to broadened the range of positions available to her students after they graduated from ENSJF, particularly in the [[Grands corps de l'État]] (French civil service) and in international positions.<ref name=":0" />

Under her leadership the École Normale for Girls merged with the École Normale Supérieure on Rue d'Ulm. The merger of the two schools took place in 1985.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> The following years were marked by transition.<ref name=":3" /> From 1988 to 1991, Serre was part of the management team of the co-educational [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]].<ref name=":3" />

In 1986, Serre recommended expanding recruitment to the [[Grande école|grandes écoles]] in a report submitted to the [[Prime Minister of France]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last= |date=14 March 1986 |title=Les grandes écoles devraient élargir leur recrutement |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1986/03/14/les-grandes-ecoles-devraient-elargir-leur-recrutement_2923032_1819218.html |journal=[[Le Monde]] |page= |issn=}}</ref>

After the death in 1989 of mathematician [[Georges Poitou]], director of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]], Serre served as interim administrator from 1989 to 1990. She was the first woman to hold this position.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hommage du comité de la Société des amis de l'ENS - 1994-2004 |url=http://bhef.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr/simple_search.php?ITHEME1=Biographie+de+professeurs+du+niveau+sup%E9rieur&order_by=_titre%2Cid&offset=986 |website=Bibliographie d'histoire de l'éducation française}}</ref> 

The same year, she was appointed to the [[AERES|Comité national d'évaluation des établissements publics à caractère scientifique, culturel et professionnel]] (National Committee for the Evaluation of Public Scientific, Cultural and Professional Institutions).<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 May 1989 |title=Les dix-sept nouveaux membres |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1989/05/19/les-dix-sept-nouveaux-membres_4143863_1819218.html |access-date=1 March 2026 |website=Le Monde}}</ref>

In 1991, she was appointed to the cabinet of the then Minister of National Education, [[Lionel Jospin]], where she was responsible for the newly established [[Institut Universitaire de Formation des Maîtres|instituts universitaires de formation des maîtres]] (university institutes for teacher training).<ref name=":2" />

== Personal life and death ==
Josiane Heulot married mathematician [[Jean-Pierre Serre]]. The couple had one daughter, [[Claudine Monteil]], [[diplomat]] and writer.<ref name=":3" /> Josiane Serre died in Paris on 11 October 2004.<ref name=":5" />

== Recognition ==

She was made an Officer of the [[Legion of Honour]] on 23 May 1989.<ref name=":3" />

In 2026, Serre was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-28 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref>
